decisions.reason: The branding identity changes, but the required full-document layout, formatting, pass count, and graphic-treatment coverage remain unchanged.
Changing the proposal branding does not alter the requirement to incorporate supplied photos into the final draft.
The organization chart must still be incorporated into the final draft; the branding shift does not change that action.
The branding decision does not remove or modify the requirement to include the budget sheet and supplied proposal tables.
The final deliverable remains a print-ready PDF regardless of whether the visual identity is GreenLatinos or Agua Arc.
The branding shift does not alter the Canva source-delivery or client-editability requirements.
All supplied narrative content must still be included; the source decision changes visual branding rather than required content coverage.
The shift to Agua Arc branding does not change the proposal's stated page-count target.

The candidate already records the same-message requirement for replaceable client attribution instead of client branding, while Agua Arc visual identity remains owned by the separate branding Requirement; no additional template-state change is necessary.
